sources.title: A Survey of Context Engineering for Large Language Models
sources.venue_or_author: Mei, Yao, Ge et al. (ICT/CAS et al.), arXiv 2507.13334
sources.summary: Formalizes 'context engineering' as a discipline beyond prompt design: a taxonomy of foundational components (context retrieval/generation, processing, management) and system implementations (RAG, memory systems, tool-integrated reasoning, multi-agent). Built from ~1,400 papers; flags the asymmetry between models' ability to understand long context vs. generate long, coherent outputs.
sources.popularity_signal: 143 citations (Semantic Scholar, Aug 2026); companion repo Meirtz/Awesome-Context-Engineering

sources.title: Awesome-Context-Engineering (companion paper list to the Mei et al. survey)
sources.venue_or_author: Meirtz (Lingrui Mei) on GitHub
sources.summary: Curated, continuously updated list of hundreds of papers, frameworks and implementation guides organized under the survey's taxonomy (retrieval, processing, management, RAG, memory, multi-agent).
sources.popularity_signal: stars not captured; the canonical companion repo of the 2507.13334 survey

sources.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
sources.venue_or_author: Packer, Wooders, Lin et al. (UC Berkeley), arXiv 2310.08560
sources.summary: Introduces virtual context management: an OS-inspired memory hierarchy (in-context 'main context' vs. out-of-context 'external context') where the LLM pages information in and out via function calls and interrupts, yielding effectively unbounded context for document analysis and multi-session chat. Basis of the Letta framework.

sources.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
sources.venue_or_author: Park, O'Brien, Cai, Morris, Liang, Bernstein (Stanford/Google), UIST 2023
sources.summary: Agents keep a natural-language memory stream of all experiences, periodically synthesize higher-level reflections, and retrieve memories scored by recency, importance and relevance to plan behavior; demonstrated in a 25-agent sandbox town. The archetype for retrieval-plus-reflection agent memory.

sources.title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
sources.venue_or_author: Xu, Liang, Mei et al. (Rutgers et al.), NeurIPS 2025
sources.summary: Zettelkasten-inspired memory: each experience becomes an atomic note with contextual description, keywords and tags; new notes are linked to related ones and can trigger updates of existing notes (memory evolution), enabling dynamic structured organization instead of fixed memory schemas.

sources.title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
sources.venue_or_author: Chhikara, Khant, Aryan, Singh, Yadav (Mem0), ECAI 2025
sources.summary: Memory-centric architecture that dynamically extracts, consolidates and retrieves salient facts from conversations (plus a graph-memory variant); on LOCOMO it beats OpenAI memory, RAG, and full-context baselines while cutting p95 latency ~91% and token cost ~90% relative to full-context.
sources.popularity_signal: 559 citations (Semantic Scholar); backs the mem0 open-source library

sources.title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
sources.venue_or_author: Zhong, Guo, Gao, Ye, Wang, AAAI 2024
sources.summary: Adds a long-term memory store that lets an LLM recall relevant past interactions, continually update a user portrait, and forget/strengthen memories following the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve; demonstrated via the SiliconFriend companion chatbot.

sources.title: Recursively Summarizing Enables Long-Term Dialogue Memory in Large Language Models
sources.venue_or_author: Wang et al., Neurocomputing 2025 (arXiv 2308.15022)
sources.summary: Maintains a running memory by having the LLM summarize small dialogue chunks and then recursively fold previous memory plus new turns into an updated summary, improving consistency in long conversations with ChatGPT/text-davinci-003. The canonical 'summary-buffer' approach.

sources.title: A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of Large Language Model-based Agents
sources.venue_or_author: Zhang, Bo, Ma et al. (Renmin Univ.), ACM TOIS 2025
sources.summary: Systematically surveys what memory is for LLM agents, why it is needed, and how to design it: memory sources, forms (textual vs. parametric), and operations (writing, management, reading), with evaluation methods and application areas.

sources.title: From Human Memory to AI Memory: A Survey on Memory Mechanisms in the Era of LLMs
sources.venue_or_author: Wu et al. (Huawei Noah's Ark Lab), arXiv 2504.15965
sources.summary: Maps human-memory concepts onto LLM memory and proposes a 3D-8Q taxonomy (object, form, time x eight quadrants) to classify memory mechanisms, with open problems for personal assistants and agents.

sources.title: On Memory Construction and Retrieval for Personalized Conversational Agents (SeCom)
sources.venue_or_author: Pan et al. (Microsoft), ICLR 2025
sources.summary: Studies memory granularity (turn vs. session vs. summary) and shows topically segmented memory units plus LLMLingua-2-style compression denoising improve retrieval and response quality on LOCOMO and Long-MT-Bench+.

sources.title: The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management
sources.venue_or_author: Lindenbauer, Slinko, Felder, Bogomolov, Zharov (JetBrains Research), arXiv 2508.21433
sources.summary: On SWE-bench Verified coding agents, simply masking/eliding old tool observations cuts cost by roughly half and matches or beats LLM-based summarization of the trajectory; summarization can even prolong trajectories. Argues for simple baselines before complex compaction.

sources.title: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models
sources.venue_or_author: Jiang, Wu, Lin, Yang, Qiu (Microsoft), EMNLP 2023
sources.summary: Coarse-to-fine prompt compression: a small LM scores token importance by perplexity, a budget controller allocates compression across demonstrations/instructions/questions, and iterative token-level compression yields up to 20x compression with little performance loss.

sources.title: LongLLMLingua: Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression
sources.venue_or_author: Jiang, Wu, Luo et al. (Microsoft), ACL 2024
sources.summary: Question-aware coarse-to-fine compression plus reordering of documents to counter lost-in-the-middle; boosts GPT-3.5-Turbo on NaturalQuestions by up to 21.4% with ~4x fewer tokens and lower latency/cost.

sources.title: LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression
sources.venue_or_author: Pan, Wu, Jiang et al. (Microsoft/Tsinghua), ACL 2024 Findings
sources.summary: Distills GPT-4 compression decisions into a dataset and trains a small bidirectional token-classifier (XLM-RoBERTa) to keep/drop tokens; task-agnostic, 3-6x faster than LLMLingua with 2-5x compression and up to 2.9x lower end-to-end latency.

sources.title: Prompt Compression for Large Language Models: A Survey
sources.venue_or_author: Li, Liu, Buck, Collier (Cambridge), NAACL 2025
sources.summary: Surveys prompt compression as hard-prompt (filtering/paraphrasing tokens, e.g. LLMLingua, Selective Context) vs. soft-prompt (learned compressed vectors, e.g. gist tokens, AutoCompressors, ICAE) methods, and discusses mechanisms, benchmarks and open challenges.

sources.title: Learning to Compress Prompts with Gist Tokens
sources.venue_or_author: Mu, Li, Goodman (Stanford), NeurIPS 2023
sources.summary: 'Gisting' trains an LM to compress a prompt into a few cacheable gist tokens by modifying attention masks during instruction tuning; up to 26x prompt compression with ~40% FLOP reduction and minimal quality loss.

sources.title: Adapting Language Models to Compress Contexts (AutoCompressors)
sources.venue_or_author: Chevalier, Wettig, Ajith, Chen (Princeton), EMNLP 2023
sources.summary: AutoCompressors fine-tune LMs to recursively compress long documents into compact summary vectors used as soft prompts, extending effective context and improving retrieval-augmented LM / in-context learning at lower compute.

sources.title: In-context Autoencoder for Context Compression in a Large Language Model (ICAE)
sources.venue_or_author: Ge, Hu, Wang, Wang, Chen, Wei (Microsoft), ICLR 2024
sources.summary: A LoRA-adapted encoder compresses long context into short 'memory slots' that the frozen target LLM conditions on; pretrained with autoencoding + LM objectives, achieving ~4x compression with latency and GPU memory savings.

sources.title: Unlocking Context Constraints of LLMs: Self-Information-Based Content Filtering (Selective Context)
sources.venue_or_author: Yucheng Li (Univ. of Surrey), arXiv 2304.12102 / EMNLP 2023
sources.summary: Selective Context removes low self-information (low-surprise) lexical units from the prompt using a small causal LM, cutting context length on summarization and QA over papers, news and transcripts with modest quality loss.

sources.title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
sources.venue_or_author: Xu, Shi, Choi (UT Austin / UW), ICLR 2024
sources.summary: Compresses retrieved documents into short extractive or abstractive summaries before prepending them, and can return an empty summary to skip augmentation; keeps performance at ~6% of original tokens on LM and QA tasks.

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
sources.venue_or_author: Liu, Lin, Hewitt et al. (Stanford/UC Berkeley), TACL 2024
sources.summary: Shows a U-shaped performance curve: models use information best at the start or end of the context and degrade sharply when the relevant passage is in the middle, even for explicitly long-context models; motivates reordering and context curation.

sources.title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
sources.venue_or_author: Hsieh, Sun, Kriman et al. (NVIDIA), COLM 2024
sources.summary: Synthetic benchmark extending needle-in-a-haystack with multi-needle, multi-hop tracing and aggregation tasks; of 17 models claiming >=32K context, only a handful kept satisfactory performance at 32K, showing advertised context sizes overstate effective context.

sources.title: LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding
sources.venue_or_author: Bai, Lv, Zhang et al. (Tsinghua/Zhipu), ACL 2024
sources.summary: First bilingual (EN/ZH) multi-task long-context benchmark: 21 tasks across single-/multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks and code completion; later extended as LongBench v2 (ACL 2025).

sources.title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
sources.venue_or_author: Hong, Troynikov, Huber (Chroma technical report, July 2025)
sources.summary: Controlled experiments on 18 frontier models (GPT-4.1, Claude 4, Gemini 2.5, Qwen3) show reliability degrades non-uniformly as input grows, even on simple retrieval and text-replication tasks; coined 'context rot' and is widely used to justify context curation over maximal stuffing.
sources.popularity_signal: widely referenced technical report; replication toolkit at github.com/chroma-core/context-rot

sources.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs? A Comprehensive Study and Hybrid Approach
sources.venue_or_author: Li, Liu, Mi, Zheng, Bendersky (Google DeepMind), EMNLP 2024 Industry
sources.summary: Benchmarks RAG vs. long-context prompting with Gemini-1.5/GPT-4o: long context wins on average when affordable, RAG is far cheaper; proposes Self-Route, which lets the model decide per query whether retrieval suffices, matching LC quality at much lower cost.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
sources.venue_or_author: Gao, Xiong, Gao et al. (Tongji/Fudan), arXiv 2312.10997
sources.summary: The standard RAG survey: organizes methods into naive, advanced and modular RAG, covering retrieval, generation and augmentation techniques plus evaluation frameworks and benchmarks.
sources.popularity_signal: unknown (not captured; among the most-cited RAG surveys)

sources.title: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey on Agentic RAG
sources.venue_or_author: Singh, Ehtesham, Kumar, Khoei, arXiv 2501.09136
sources.summary: Surveys Agentic RAG, where autonomous agents plan, reflect, use tools and collaborate inside the retrieval pipeline; proposes a taxonomy (single-agent, multi-agent, hierarchical, corrective, adaptive, graph-based) with applications and open challenges.

sources.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Long Context Language Modeling
sources.venue_or_author: Liu et al. (multi-institution), arXiv 2503.17407
sources.summary: Broad survey of long-context LMs covering data, architectures (position encodings, efficient attention), training, inference (KV cache, compression), evaluation benchmarks and applications, including a section on context compression and agent memory.

sources.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks (StreamingLLM)
sources.venue_or_author: Xiao, Tian, Chen, Han, Lewis (MIT/Meta), ICLR 2024
sources.summary: Observes that initial tokens act as 'attention sinks'; keeping their KV states plus a sliding window of recent tokens lets finite-window LLMs model streams of 4M+ tokens stably without fine-tuning, with up to 22x speedup over recomputation.

sources.title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
sources.venue_or_author: Zhang, Sheng, Zhou et al. (UT Austin/Stanford/Meta), NeurIPS 2023
sources.summary: Shows a small set of 'heavy hitter' tokens dominate attention mass; a dynamic eviction policy keeping recent tokens plus heavy hitters shrinks the KV cache (e.g. 20% budget) with negligible loss and up to 29x throughput gains.

sources.title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
sources.venue_or_author: Li, Huang, Yang et al. (UIUC/Cohere), NeurIPS 2024
sources.summary: Fine-tuning-free method that uses an observation window at the end of the prompt to pick, per attention head, the important prefix KV positions before decoding; 3.6x faster generation and 8.2x memory efficiency on 16K inputs with comparable accuracy.

sources.title: PyramidKV: Dynamic KV Cache Compression based on Pyramidal Information Funneling
sources.venue_or_author: Cai, Zhang, Gao et al. (PKU et al.), arXiv 2406.02069
sources.summary: Finds attention is diffuse in lower layers and concentrated in upper layers ('information funneling'), so allocates more KV budget to lower layers and less to upper ones; matches full-cache LongBench accuracy with ~12% of the KV cache.

sources.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache
sources.venue_or_author: Liu, Yuan, Jin et al. (Rice/Univ. of Illinois), ICML 2024
sources.summary: Tuning-free 2-bit KV quantization that quantizes keys per-channel and values per-token based on their distributions; Llama-2/Falcon/Mistral keep quality with 2.6x lower peak memory, enabling 4x larger batches and 2.35-3.47x throughput.

sources.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models
sources.venue_or_author: Peng, Quesnelle, Fan, Shippole (Nous Research/EleutherAI), ICLR 2024
sources.summary: Extends RoPE models' context (e.g. LLaMA to 128K) with NTK-by-parts frequency interpolation plus attention-logit temperature scaling, needing ~10x fewer tokens and 2.5x fewer training steps than prior interpolation methods.

sources.title: Leave No Context Behind: Efficient Infinite Context Transformers with Infini-attention
sources.venue_or_author: Munkhdalai, Faruqui, Gopal (Google), arXiv 2404.07143
sources.summary: Adds a compressive memory with linear-attention retrieval inside each attention block, combining masked local attention and long-term memory so Transformers process unbounded streams with bounded memory; 114x memory compression on 1M-token passkey and 500K book summarization.

sources.title: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context
sources.venue_or_author: Liu, Zaharia, Abbeel (UC Berkeley), ICLR 2024
sources.summary: Distributes a long sequence across devices in a ring, overlapping KV-block communication with blockwise attention/feed-forward computation, enabling context length to scale linearly with device count without approximation; underpins 1M+-token training.

sources.title: The Missing Memory Hierarchy: Demand Paging for LLM Context Windows
sources.venue_or_author: arXiv 2603.09023 (authors not captured)
sources.summary: Argues the context window should sit atop an explicit memory hierarchy with OS-style demand paging of context in and out rather than ad-hoc truncation (title/abstract-level; full text not fetched).

sources.title: TokenPilot: Cache-Efficient Context Management for LLM Agents
sources.venue_or_author: arXiv 2606.17016 (authors not captured)
sources.summary: Context-management scheme for agents that edits/compacts the working context while keeping prompt-cache prefix hits, trading off context size against cache reuse cost (title/abstract-level; full text not fetched).

sources.title: Hold Onto That Thought: Assessing KV Cache Compression On Reasoning
sources.summary: Evaluates eviction and quantization KV-compression methods on long chain-of-thought reasoning models, showing that methods tuned on standard long-context tasks can break multi-step reasoning and that accumulated-attention heavy-hitter strategies hold up best.

sources.title: U-NIAH: Unified RAG and LLM Evaluation for Long Context Needle-In-A-Haystack
sources.venue_or_author: ACM TOIS 2025 (arXiv 2503.00353)
sources.summary: Unified needle-in-a-haystack framework that evaluates long-context LLMs and RAG pipelines side by side across needle types/positions, quantifying when retrieval beats raw long context and vice versa.

sources.title: A Survey on the Security of Long-Term Memory in LLM Agents: Toward Mnemonic Sovereignty
sources.summary: Surveys attacks and defenses on persistent agent memory (poisoning, extraction, tampering) and argues for 'mnemonic sovereignty'; relevant as OWASP's 2026 Agentic Top 10 lists memory and context poisoning.
